clue.text: Magazine articles that could do a lot of damage

definitions.text: Magazine articles that could do a lot of damage

parts.words: Magazine articles that could do a lot of damage
parts.note: read 'magazine' not as a periodical but as a store of ammunition: the items kept in it for a gun are what does the damage

explanation.surface: A complaint that certain features in a periodical are dangerously harmful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Magazine' suggests a publication and 'articles' its pieces of writing, but a magazine is also a place where explosives and ammunition are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Gunpowder and lead pellets were the ammunition for old firearms, the stock a military magazine held.

clue.text: Talk on about proportional representation

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word for 'on' is placed around the other piece

parts.note: taken as written
a ratio expresses how one quantity is represented in proportion to another

explanation.surface: A speech given on the subject of the voting system known as proportional representation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Proportional representation' looks like the electoral system but is just defining RATIO; 'about' puts ON around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal speech or address delivered to an audience is a kind of talk.

clue.text: Spot a weak type

explanation.surface: Reads like a remark identifying a feeble person on sight.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a single falling drop of liquid; the other is slang for a feeble, spineless person.

clue.text: Tracks for athletes

explanation.surface: Sounds like a note about running tracks laid out for sportspeople.
explanation.definitionFit: Grooves or rails along which drawers or sledges slide are so called; competitors in races are also so called.

clue.text: Heaven is covered transport in a rainstorm

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the other, so the vehicle goes within the stirred-up letters
a storm whips things about, so the letters of rain just before it are thrown into a new order

parts.note: a van is a covered road vehicle for carrying goods

explanation.surface: Someone joking that bliss is being dry inside a lorry during a downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'storm' is the second half of 'rainstorm': it scrambles RAIN into NIRA, and 'in' places VAN inside that, after NIR.
explanation.definitionFit: In Buddhism this is the state of perfect bliss and release, used loosely for paradise.

clue.text: Wise cooks use it

explanation.surface: Reads like a claim that clever chefs use some ingredient.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means sagacious; as a noun it is a grey-leaved herb used in stuffing.

clue.text: Famous actor I observed in a musical

indicators.note: the letter is seen inside the show's title, so it is placed within that word

parts.note: Oliver! is Lionel Bart's stage musical based on Oliver Twist
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone boasting that they spotted a well-known performer in a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: Laurence Olivier was a celebrated English stage and film actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence, Lord Olivier was one of the most renowned British actors of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Listen to the complete record; impartial judges must

explanation.surface: A comparison between playing an entire LP and the duty of a fair judge.
explanation.definitionFit: A vinyl record has an A side and a B side; a fair arbiter must also attend to the case for each party.

clue.text: One who informs a referee?

explanation.surface: Asks whether an informant could be someone officiating a match.
explanation.definitionFit: An informer exposing wrongdoing is so called; literally, a match official is someone who sounds a whistle.

clue.text: Tail one wags in delight

indicators.note: wagging moves a thing to and fro, so the letters of the two preceding words are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A dog wagging its tail out of happiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wags' rearranges TAILONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Elation is a feeling of great joy or exhilaration, a synonym for this sense of happiness.

clue.text: Arch is rough cast on the outside

indicators.note: the jumbled letters sit on the outside, wrapping around the short word inside them
casting something throws it, so the letters of rough are thrown into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A description of an architectural arch finished in rough render on its exterior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' turns ROUGH into ROGUH, and 'on the outside' puts that around IS. 'Arch' is the adjective meaning playfully mischievous, not a curved structure.
explanation.definitionFit: An arch smile or look is mischievous and knowing, the same as one that is playfully impish.

clue.text: Bird run over by train

explanation.surface: A grim news item about a bird struck by a railway engine.
explanation.definitionFit: A rail is a marsh bird like the water rail; a steel bar of track is what a locomotive's wheels pass over.

clue.text: Those who start such a race never finish

definitions.text: Those who start such a race never finish

parts.words: Those who start such a race never finish
parts.note: in a team race run in legs, the opening runner hands the baton on and someone else crosses the line

explanation.surface: A gloomy statement about runners who quit before the end.
explanation.walkthrough: It sounds like a remark about failure, but in a team race the first leg runner never crosses the finish line by design.
explanation.definitionFit: A team race in which each member runs one stage and passes on a baton is so called.

clue.text: Fail to get a girl's address

explanation.surface: Reads like being unable to find out where a young woman lives.
explanation.definitionFit: To fail to catch or hit is one sense; the other is the polite title used before an unmarried woman's name.

clue.text: Sailor has half a bottle with a male superior

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is the usual abbreviation for a sailor

indicators.note: half of the six-letter word bottle is taken, its first three letters

explanation.surface: A seaman sharing a drink from a half-empty bottle with a senior monk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half a bottle' takes the first half of BOTTLE, BOT.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a community of monks is the masculine counterpart of an abbess.

clue.text: It may be smoked out of its den

definitions.text: It may be smoked out of its den

parts.words: It may be smoked out of its den
parts.note: sounds like an animal driven from its lair by smoke, but means a drug consumed in a den kept for it

explanation.surface: Describes a fox or badger being smoked out of its burrow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smoked out' suggests forcing an animal from its lair; here the drug is smoked, out of (from) the den where users gather.
explanation.definitionFit: A narcotic from poppies, traditionally smoked in dens set aside for its users.

clue.text: Large volume of transport?

explanation.surface: Asks whether a big book counts as a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A single book collecting several works is one sense; the old word for a bus is the other.

clue.text: Garments appear dishevelled on student

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it
something dishevelled is messed up, so the letters of appear are put in disorder

parts.note: L, for a learner driver's plate, is the usual abbreviation for a student

explanation.surface: Clothes look scruffy when worn by an untidy student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dishevelled' rearranges APPEAR into APPARE; 'on' puts it before L.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparel is a formal word for clothing, matching this plural sense.

clue.text: The bed of the sea

parts.note: looks like the ocean floor, but means the hanging sleeping place of a seaman aboard ship

explanation.surface: Appears to describe the seabed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed of the sea' suggests the seafloor; it is the sailors' bed at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors traditionally slept in slung canvas beds strung between beams below deck.

clue.text: Poor visibility-beginnings of rain and light wind

parts.note: mist is a light fog that reduces how far one can see

indicators.note: the beginnings are the first letters of each of the three words that follow

explanation.surface: A weather report: fog, then the start of drizzle and a gentle breeze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light wind' looks like a breeze, but 'light' gives L and 'wind' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The mistral is a cold northerly wind blowing down the Rhône valley into southern France.

clue.text: A royal estate

parts.note: a monarch's domain, the whole realm being the estate a ruler holds

explanation.walkthrough: 'estate' suggests a country house and grounds; the whole land ruled by a monarch is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm ruled by a monarch is so called, the territory over which a crowned head reigns.

clue.text: Stems from theatrical conversation

explanation.surface: Suggests some trait arising out of dialogue on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant's edible pink stalks are one sense; the word extras mutter to imitate background chatter on stage is the other.

clue.text: Troops didn't finish the course

indicators.note: not finishing means the final letter of the word for troops is dropped

parts.note: a regiment is a body of troops

explanation.surface: Soldiers who failed to complete their training programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' is not a training course but a course of treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: A prescribed course of diet, exercise or medical treatment is a regimen.

clue.text: Substandard may mean a small reduction in price

explanation.surface: Suggests a shop marking down slightly faulty goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, something not quite right or unacceptable is described this way; literally it is a slight discount.

clue.text: Cut down this month, in a way

parts.note: taken as written
ST, for street, is a common abbreviation for a way or road

explanation.surface: Someone trimming expenses this month by some method.
explanation.walkthrough: In old business letters 'inst.' (short for instant) means of the current month; 'cut down' signals that shortened form.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation for instant, a dated commercial term referring to the present month.

clue.text: They're not expected to get a horse on board

indicators.note: being on a ship means being inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: in crosswords, board stands for a ship, SS being steamship
a nag is an old or worn-out horse

explanation.surface: Unlikely candidates to get a horse taken aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is a standard crossword signal for putting something inside SS, the steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: Snags are unforeseen difficulties or hitches that crop up.

clue.text: Storage for crude oils

indicators.note: crude means rough or unrefined, so the letters of oils are put in a rough new order

explanation.surface: A tank for keeping unrefined oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crude oils' looks like petroleum but 'crude' rearranges OILS.
explanation.definitionFit: A silo is a tower or pit for storing grain, fodder or missiles.

clue.text: Avoid getting hot in a blazer

indicators.note: in shows one piece placed inside the other

parts.note: the sun is something that blazes
H is the standard abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Advice to stay away from overheating in a jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blazer' looks like a jacket but means something that blazes, the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: To shun someone or something is to keep away from them deliberately.

clue.text: Lacking lustre a sailor is under the doctor

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece that is under another is written after it

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is the usual abbreviation for a sailor

explanation.surface: A dull seaman being treated by a physician.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, AB 'under' DR follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dull and colourless is drab, without shine or brightness.

clue.text: Had tree replaced, safe from lightning

indicators.note: the letters are put back in different places, so the two preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone had a tree moved so it would no longer attract lightning strikes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced' rearranges HADTREE.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrical equipment connected to the ground by a conductor is protected from strikes and shocks.

clue.text: New moral we find in old writer

indicators.note: new indicates the letters of the following words made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A fresh ethical lesson found in the work of a classic author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges MORALWE. Christopher Marlowe was an Elizabethan playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Marlowe, author of Doctor Faustus, was an Elizabethan dramatist and poet.

clue.text: Not everyone sees the fun in this party game

definitions.text: Not everyone sees the fun in this party game

parts.words: Not everyone sees the fun in this party game
parts.note: playful wording: one player is blindfolded, so literally cannot see while the others enjoy themselves

explanation.surface: A grumble that some guests do not enjoy a certain party game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not everyone sees the fun' sounds like some find it boring, but in this game one player is blindfolded and literally cannot see.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's game where a blindfolded player tries to catch and identify the others.
